meta.scope: Taiwan Batch 3 — Monetary & financial conditions (CBC), long-term care / ageing social response, energy balance & electricity generation mix (nuclear share now very low), and supporting social/structural nodes. Explicit referenced_by lists retained for force-layout edge strength.
meta.strategy_note: Continues edge-conscious mining. Taiwan’s energy profile (nuclear share collapsed to low single digits) forms a useful contrast cluster with Korea’s high nuclear share. Long-term care and monetary series tighten the demographic and financial clusters.

candidates.title: Monetary Aggregates (M1B, M2) and Financial Conditions
candidates.publisher: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan)
candidates.description: Monthly statistics on monetary aggregates (M1B, M2), loans and investments of financial institutions, and related financial-conditions indicators. Core high-frequency monetary data released by the CBC.
candidates.notes: Parallel to Korea’s M1/M2/Lf series and Japan’s monetary aggregates. Tight edges into CBC institutional node, interest-rate policy and credit conditions.

candidates.title: Foreign Exchange Reserves
candidates.publisher: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan)
candidates.description: Monthly official foreign-exchange reserve holdings. Taiwan maintains one of the world’s largest reserve stocks relative to GDP, reflecting persistent current-account surpluses.
referenced_by: Balance of Payments and international investment position
CBC annual reports and financial-conditions releases
candidates.notes: High-authority external-strength node. Creates strong edges from the large BOP current-account surplus into reserve accumulation.

candidates.title: Long-Term Care services and statistics (Long-Term Care Services Act framework)
candidates.publisher: Ministry of Health and Welfare / Ministry of Finance statistics / related agencies
candidates.description: Statistics on long-term care service units (institutional, home-based, community-based), utilisation, and the policy framework established under the Long-Term Care Services Act. Number of registered units has risen sharply as Taiwan entered super-aged status.
referenced_by: Super-aged society indicators and population projections
Ageing-society white papers and policy evaluations
candidates.notes: Social-response node to the demographic extremes already captured. Parallel to Japan’s LTCI and Korea’s Long-Term Care Insurance series. Strengthens the ageing–care cluster.

candidates.title: Energy Statistics Handbook / Energy balance and electricity generation mix
candidates.publisher: Energy Administration, Ministry of Economic Affairs
candidates.description: Annual and periodic energy statistics covering primary energy supply, transformation, final consumption, and detailed electricity generation by source (coal, gas, nuclear, renewables). Nuclear share has fallen to low single digits in recent years.
referenced_by: Industrial production and energy-intensive manufacturing analysis
candidates.notes: Critical contrast node. Unlike Korea’s ~32 % nuclear share, Taiwan’s nuclear contribution has declined sharply; gas and renewables have risen. Creates a distinctive energy-cluster signature relative to both Japan and Korea.

candidates.title: Nuclear power status and phase-out / life-extension policy statistics
candidates.publisher: Atomic Energy Council / Energy Administration / related agencies
candidates.description: Statistics and policy tracking of Taiwan’s nuclear fleet capacity, generation share, and the political/regulatory trajectory of phase-out versus possible life-extension or restart debates.
referenced_by: Energy Statistics Handbook and electricity generation mix
candidates.notes: Uniqueness node. The near-phase-out trajectory (nuclear share now ~1–4 %) is a defining energy-policy feature and produces clear edges into the broader energy and industrial-cost clusters.

candidates.title: Family Income and Expenditure Survey / Household income statistics
candidates.description: Periodic survey of household income, expenditure, savings and distribution. Source for inequality, consumption and living-standards analysis.
candidates.notes: Core household survey parallel to Japan and Korea counterparts. Strengthens income–distribution and living-conditions edges.

candidates.title: Labour productivity and unit labour cost statistics
candidates.description: Statistics on labour productivity and unit labour costs, particularly for the industrial and manufacturing sectors. Closely watched given the high productivity growth in electronics and semiconductors.
candidates.notes: Links the semiconductor/industrial cluster to labour and cost competitiveness. Useful for force-layout connections between real-activity and cost nodes.

candidates.title: Construction and housing statistics
candidates.publisher: DGBAS / Ministry of the Interior / related agencies
candidates.description: Statistics on construction activity, building permits, housing stock and related real-estate indicators.
candidates.notes: Supporting structural node that feeds investment and regional clusters.

candidates.title: Education statistics (enrolment, schools, attainment)
candidates.description: Statistics on schools, student enrolment, educational attainment and related human-capital indicators. Interacts with demographic decline (shrinking school-age cohorts) and high-tech labour demand.
candidates.notes: Human-capital node that bridges demographic decline and the high-tech industrial cluster.

candidates.title: Financial Stability Report / banking and systemic-risk statistics
candidates.publisher: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan) / Financial Supervisory Commission
candidates.description: Periodic Financial Stability Report and underlying statistics on bank soundness, household and corporate credit, real-estate exposure and systemic-risk indicators.
candidates.notes: Deepens the financial cluster. Parallel to Korea’s Financial Stability Report node.
